analysis: The code checks that lastIndexOfDot >= 0 before calling substring. The beginIndex is lastIndexOfDot + 1, which is always >=1 and <= length of the string (since lastIndexOfDot is at most length-1). Therefore, beginIndex is never negative and never greater than length, so IndexOutOfBoundsException is avoided.
remark: Since the if condition ensures that a dot exists, the beginIndex is always a valid index (1 to length inclusive), so no exception occurs.
